title: High degrees and dominating functions

based_on.title: Lecture notes in Computability Theory
based_on.pages: Theorem 41.1, p. 109; finite-race and empty-maximum details expanded here

summary: Characterize high Turing degrees by the ability to compute one function eventually dominating every ordinary computable function.
abstract: An oracle is high when its halting problem can compute the halting problem for ordinary halting itself. This jump comparison has a concrete equivalent: the oracle computes one total numerical function that eventually bounds each ordinary computable function. A relative approximation to the totality problem supplies the forward construction. Its finite races either obtain a computation value or withdraw a mistaken guess, so their maximum always finishes. In the other direction, finite computation deadlines turn a dominating function into convergent totality guesses. The relative limit lemma connects both algorithms to the jump. Highness consequently implies hyperimmune degree, while the existing low simple set separates the two notions. Ordinary jump inversion gives further high examples, with a different upper bound from an incomplete high enumerable construction.
